skill.name: find-skills
skill.description: Search public AI skill registries from one command, compare native popularity signals, flag installed skills, and run heuristic safety checks on top candidates.
skill.summary: Find relevant Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skills across public registries.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms limited network access to public skill registries and raw skill bodies, plus local hidden-directory enumeration for installed-skill matching. Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, safe Bash command substitutions, /dev/null redirects, or grep patterns that detect secrets in candidate skill text.

remediation.issue: Search queries are sent to public registries and GitHub endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external services clearly and warn users not to search with sensitive project or client names.

remediation.issue: The script reads hidden local skill directories to detect installed skills.
remediation.suggestion: Add a flag to disable installed-skill discovery, or ask before reading local skill folders.

remediation.issue: Candidate skill bodies and clawhub archives are downloaded for heuristic scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Keep downloads read-only, enforce size limits, and continue avoiding execution of downloaded content.

content.value_statement: AI skill discovery is fragmented across registries and GitHub topics. This skill searches them together, compares native signals, and highlights safety warnings before installation.
actual_capabilities: Searches skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub topic results for a user query.
Shows source health, result counts, latency, and local installed-skill matches.
Ranks each source with its native metric, such as installs or stars.
Fetches top candidate skill bodies and flags risky patterns heuristically.
Outputs formatted recommendations or machine-readable JSON.
Handles missing optional tools with partial results when possible.
limitations: Requires curl and jq; GitHub and clawhub body scans need optional tools.
Sends the search query to public registries and GitHub APIs.
Security scan is heuristic and does not replace manual review.
GitHub results depend on topic tags, so untagged repositories may be missed.

use_cases.title: Choose a Skill for a New Task
use_cases.description: Search multiple registries, compare popularity signals, and recommend one fitting skill.

use_cases.title: Audit Skill Options Before Install
use_cases.description: Review candidate metadata, installed status, and heuristic risk flags before installation.

use_cases.title: Research Marketplace Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub coverage for a capability area.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-skills to search for a skill that helps with {task}. Show the strongest recommendation and one alternative.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Adjacent Terms
prompt_templates.scenario: Broaden discovery when one query may miss good matches.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run find-skills for {term_one}, {term_two}, and {term_three}. Pool the results and recommend one skill with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Vet Before Install
prompt_templates.scenario: Check safety flags before suggesting an installation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for {task}, scan top candidates, and explain any caution or risky flags before suggesting installation.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Marketplace Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison using all available signals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use find-skills with structured output for {task}. Compare registry popularity, GitHub maintenance, installed status, and safety flags, then produce a final install recommendation.

output_examples.input: Find a skill for browser testing.
output_examples.output: The response names a primary recommendation, explains why it fits, lists one alternative, and notes any safety badge.

output_examples.input: Check whether I already have a PDF workflow skill.
output_examples.output: The response marks matching installed skills, explains whether installation is needed, and shows registry alternatives.

output_examples.input: Find deployment skills but avoid risky installs.
output_examples.output: The response excludes risky candidates, explains caution flags, and recommends a safer install path when available.

best_practices: Run two or three adjacent searches before deciding.
Read the top candidate SKILL.md or README before recommending.
Treat a clean scan as a heuristic and review permissions manually.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend from install counts alone.
Do not install a risky result without explicit user acceptance.
Do not treat GitHub topic results as complete registry coverage.

faq.question: Which sources does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches skills.sh, clawhub.ai, and GitHub repositories tagged with common skill topics.

faq.question: Does it install skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It only recommends options and shows install guidance after review.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: The search query is sent to public registries and GitHub APIs when the script runs.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: curl and jq are required. gh and unzip improve GitHub search and candidate scanning.

faq.question: Is the security scan a full audit?
faq.answer: No. It is a heuristic scan for common risky patterns and still requires manual review.

faq.question: Can it detect installed skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks local agent skill directories and matches folder names against search results.
